# testkit

## Maturity

**Grade:** 1 · S1 E1 A1 H1 P1 *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** ahead — Zig 0.17 `std.testing` (extended), against proptest/Hypothesis (shrinking), insta (goldens), criterion and `testing.B` (bench skeleton, `benchkit` since 2026-11-14) for the pieces this module carries; typed strategies (`arbitrary`, 2026-11-13) are here as a mapping from types, without combinators; inline snapshots with an update workflow are here (2026-11-15; no review mode); bench statistics, regex string strategies and stateful testing are documented gaps (Backlog) (surveyed 2026-10-17; shrinking measured against proptest 1.11.0 and libFuzzer 2026-10-27: parity, plus the lead on the `**Ahead:**` line; Hypothesis, the design reference, and rapid not measured)

**Ahead:** feature — a shrunk failure is the failure that was found, where proptest and libFuzzer slip to a different bug: a constructed worst case, a `Deep` bug (≥ 16 bytes summing to ≥ 1500) next to a `Shallow` one (a leading zero byte, which zeroing — a step every shrinker takes — walks into), over 20 seeds each. The shrinker ends on a 16-byte `Deep` input 20 of 20 times (errors are told apart by name, faults by their signal). proptest 1.11.0 (default `Config`) reports the `Shallow` bug 20 of 20 times (its `shrink` takes any `Fail`; 1.12.0's is the same, read). libFuzzer 21.1.8 `-minimize_crash=1`, for crashes that are plain signals (`abort` / `__builtin_trap`), reports a 2-byte `Shallow` crash 20 of 20 times: plain and with ASan no `DEDUP_TOKEN` is printed (both empty, so equal), with ASan `dedup_token_length=3` the token is its own three crash-handler frames; only with ASan and a non-default `dedup_token_length=10` does it keep `Deep`, stopping at the first slip (16–24 bytes). A sanitizer report (ASan OOB, UAF) carries the bug's own frames and was not measured. Two different panics still look alike here (SIGABRT both; Backlog) (test `lead: a Deep input shrinks to a Deep input, never to the Shallow bug next to it`; `tools/slip.sh`) (measured 2026-10-27)

**Audit:** review 2026-11-13 · mutation 2026-11-15 (396/414, 18 eq) · src 8b063f07e9149772

**Hardening:** fuzz 2026-10-17 (TESTKIT_FUZZ, clean: hex 2M, golden 1M, fault 1.6M, tape 240k runs; 5 planted mutants all killed) · ct n/a — test helpers (keyword review, 2026-10-07) · panic 2026-10-29 (sweep of every pub entry point + blind review: env/file inputs capped, saturating deadlines, checked panics for caller ranges, foreign bench runs capped and timed out)

**Performance:** ref 0.24–0.48× proptest 1.11.0 · fastest 1.03× libFuzzer (LLVM 21, in-process, the property kept out of its instrumentation — libFuzzer at its cheapest; per input over the same hex property, `alloc+seedfile` the worst row; both sides JCC-padded, `-Djcc-safe`; the driver alone 0.98–1.06× a bare seed loop) (measured 2026-10-27)

**Evidence:** model-fuzz — `hex` against a from-scratch nibble decoder, golden `diff`/`render`/verdicts against a naive first-difference scan and a string-built rendering, the fault transports against their input, the choice tape against the PRNG it records (`src/fuzz_test.zig`); hex also against a strict RFC 4648 decoder over all 16276 short inputs (tools)
**Model:** src/fuzz_test.zig:nibble · tools/oracle.py

**Known defects:** none recorded

**Downstream consumer:** yes

The harness pieces every module's tests were re-deriving. **Test-only**: it is
wired into each consumer's test binary through `build.zig`'s `test_deps`, never
into the module a downstream user imports — `@import("frost")` does not drag a
test harness along with it.

- **Status:** complete. **Platform:** any.
- **Deps:** none (std only).
- **Model after:** `std.testing`, extended with the helpers this repo's own
  tests kept re-deriving.

A failing seed is then **shrunk** on a recorded tape of draws (block deletes, zeroing, binary-search lowering, whole-slice cuts), every candidate in a forked child, accepted when the outcome class is the same (the error by name / the signal, a fault keeping its own / leak / hang), and ends in a traced replay of every draw plus an in-process `<PREFIX>_CHOICES=<file>` replay. ## What is here, and why only this

Everything in this module was **measurably** duplicated first. It is not a
place to put things a test might one day want.

| Piece | Was duplicated |
|---|---|
| `verboseSkip` / `skip` | 42 byte-identical copies across 26 modules |
| `hex.bytes` | 18 byte-identical copies across 8 modules |
| `expectHex` / `expectBytes` | every `goldens.zig` spelled it differently |
| `expectSnapshot` / `expectSnapshotHex` | not duplicated: added on request (2026-11-15) — the update workflow (insta/ohsnap) that hand-edited hex goldens lack |
| `loopbackSkip` | the hand-written "loopback bind failed, skipping" give-up in ~25 modules (2026-10-01) |
| `fuzz.driver.run` / `fuzz.Rng` / `fuzz.driver.hit` | the deterministic fuzz driver, copied by hand into seglog and zstd (2026-09-27) before the web-server consumer needed it a third time |
| `stackprobe.Probe` | the dead-stack probe engine, copied into 55 modules' `stackprobe_test.zig` (27.8k lines, 2026-10-09) with hand-derived needles for every intermediate secret; this one needs none — residue below the burn is found without needles, and only secret inputs/`out` buffers are needles |
| `guard.Guarded` | brotli's input-at-a-PROT_NONE-page buffer (2026-10-15), the instrument the guard-page fuzz rule (owner rule) asks every `[*]`-reading decoder for |

The comparison bench driver (`bench`) moved to [`benchkit`](../benchkit/README.md); see "The comparison bench driver" below. Three pieces are here because the evidence asked for them rather than because they were copied: **shrinking** (every fuzz FAIL was diagnosed by hand from a whole random input), the **fault transports and allocator** (mqtt 2026-10-17: a double free visible only with a transport that fails halfway), and the shrinker's forked-child runner.

The golden comparison is the one piece that is *better* than what it replaced,
not merely shared — see below.

## What is deliberately not done

- **netns setup and privileged-capability probing.** Those read genuinely differently per module (`tc` wants a
  fresh netns with `lo` at ifindex 1; `ebpf` wants `CAP_BPF` in the *initial* user namespace, where `unshare -r`
  actively lies to you), and a shared abstraction would hide exactly the distinctions that make those skips
  correct. The VOPR side is already a module: [`netsim`](../netsim).
- **A snapshot review mode** (a `.snap.new` side file to accept or reject one by one). The in-place rewrite plus
  `git diff` / `git checkout -p` is the review the repository already has; a side file would add a second place for a
  snapshot to live in. `snapshot.zig` is a test-only file like the rest, so `check-testonly` still holds.
- **A place for things a test might one day want**: a piece is admitted only on measured duplication or on evidence (the admission rule above).

## Use

```zig
const testkit = @import("testkit");

// Skips. Returns the error, so `return` cannot fall through to the
// assertions it was meant to skip.
if (!haveCapability()) return testkit.skip("needs CAP_BPF (uid {d})", .{uid});

// A test that cannot get a loopback socket. A skip anywhere else; a FAILURE
// under scripts/lib/netns-run (ZIGLIBS_NETNS=1), where loopback is guaranteed
// and a skip would be a green run that did nothing.
const listener = addr.listen(io, .{}) catch |err|
    return testkit.loopbackSkip("loopback listen failed ({t})", .{err});

// Hex, in the three shapes the repo uses.
const key = comptime testkit.hex.bytes(32, "000102...");   // KAT vectors
const got = try testkit.hex.into(&buf, wire_hex);           // caller buffer
const owned = try testkit.hex.alloc(gpa, wire_hex);         // allocated

// Goldens.
try testkit.expectHex("45000054...", frame);
try testkit.expectBytes(expected, actual);

// Inline snapshots: the expected value is a literal right after `@src()`;
// TESTKIT_SNAPSHOT=update rewrites it.
try testkit.expectSnapshot(@src(), "HTTP/1.1 200 OK", status_line);
try testkit.expectSnapshotHex(@src(), "45000054", header);
```

## The deterministic fuzz driver

`zig build --fuzz` explores; it cannot give a verdict (no progress, exit 0 on a
crash, a hang is invisible). `fuzz.driver.run` runs the same harness over
inputs drawn from seeds, in the ordinary ReleaseSafe test binary, with a
watchdog per input:

```zig
fn harness(comptime S: type, src: *S, gpa: std.mem.Allocator) anyerror!void {
    var buf: [512]u8 = undefined;
    const n = src.slice(&buf);
    if (n > 100) testkit.fuzz.driver.hit("long input");   // reach, printed at the end
    try parse(gpa, buf[0..n]);
}
test "fuzz: the parser" {                       // exploration, optional
    try std.testing.fuzz({}, struct {
        fn f(_: void, s: *std.testing.Smith) !void { return harness(std.testing.Smith, s, std.testing.allocator); }
    }.f, .{});
}
test "fuzz driver: the parser" {                // the verdict
    try testkit.fuzz.driver.run(harness, .{ .prefix = "MOD_FUZZ", .name = "parser" });
}
test "fuzz driver: several harnesses" {        // never two `try …run(` in one test
    try testkit.fuzz.driver.runAll(.{
        .{ harness, .{ .prefix = "MOD_FUZZ", .name = "parser" } },
        .{ other, .{ .prefix = "MOD_FUZZ", .name = "parser-mutated" } },
    });
}
```

`run` skips a harness `MOD_FUZZ_ONLY` leaves out with `error.SkipZigTest`, so a
second `try run(…)` in the same test would never run; `runAll` runs each and
skips the test only when none ran (`check-skip-as-pass` refuses the chained form).

`MOD_FUZZ=<runs>[,<first seed>]` runs it (unset: skipped; a harness with `.scale = N` runs `runs / N`, so one budget suits a parser and a whole protocol exchange), `MOD_FUZZ_ONLY`
selects harnesses by name, `MOD_FUZZ_MS` is the limit per input (2000),
`MOD_FUZZ_SEEDFILE` holds the current harness and seed for a crash,
`MOD_FUZZ_INPUT` replays a saved `--fuzz` input. Output: `runs …` about once a
second, `DONE <name> runs=… in … ms`, `REACH <name> <label>=<n>`, and
`FAIL <name> seed=N: <error>` / `HANG <name> seed=N` (exit 124). One job per
core with disjoint seed ranges is the caller's runner. The source of choices
is `fuzz.Rng` — never `Smith{ .in = random bytes }`, which answers the range
minimum for almost every draw. The driver runs on 64-bit Linux
(`fuzz.driver.supported`) and skips everywhere else without compiling its
Linux code, so a module that uses it can still declare 32-bit or Windows
targets.

## Shrinking a failing seed

`FAIL`/`HANG` lines are followed by the command that shrinks them:

```
FAIL testkit-golden seed=2: TestExpectedEqual
  smallest input: TESTKIT_FUZZ_SHRINK=2 TESTKIT_FUZZ_ONLY=testkit-golden
```

`<PREFIX>_SHRINK=<seed>` reruns that seed with its choices recorded on a
**tape** (one `u64` per draw: a ranged draw's offset from its minimum, a
length, a byte, an enum's position), then tries smaller tapes — whole slices
cut (length and bytes together), blocks deleted, blocks zeroed, single
entries lowered by binary search — each in a forked child, keeping one when
it ends **the same way** (the same error, the same signal, a leak, a hang).
A panicking or hanging candidate costs a child, not the shrink. Before any
candidate, the recorded tape is replayed once and must end the same way;
otherwise the shrink stops with `error.NotReproducible` (the harness depends on
something besides its draws: an address, the clock, a counter outside the seed).
⚠ "The same signal" is compared by number: two different panics are both
SIGABRT, so a candidate may shrink one panic into another (Backlog). The result
is printed as a traced replay:

```
SHRUNK testkit-golden seed=2: 168 -> 6 choices (336 candidates)
choices: 2 1 1 4 2 1
  #0 slice[2] = 0101
  #1 fuzz_test.Mutation = .scatter
  #2 range 0..6 = 2
  #3 index <2 = 1
  ...
```

`_SHRINK_OUT=<path>` writes the tape (one number per line), `_CHOICES=<path>`
replays it in-process with every draw printed (for a debugger), `_SHRINK_MS`
is the budget (60 s). Recording lives inside `fuzz.Rng` (an optional `tape`),
not in a second source type, because 93 modules' harnesses branch on
`S == Rng` — a different type would record a different input than the one
that failed. The approach is Hypothesis's choice-sequence shrinking; no code
of it is used. In the shrinker's children core dumps are off and the debug
info is loaded once before the first fork: crashing candidates cost 0.07 s
for this module's panic test instead of 4.5 s.

## Typed values: `arbitrary`

```zig
fn harness(comptime S: type, src: *S, gpa: std.mem.Allocator) anyerror!void {
    var arena = std.heap.ArenaAllocator.init(gpa);
    defer arena.deinit();
    const req = try testkit.arbitrary(Request, S, src, arena.allocator(), .{ .bytes = .utf8 });
    try handle(req);
}
```

`arbitrary(comptime T, comptime S, src: *S, arena, comptime opts: ArbOptions) Error!T`
(`Error` is `error{OutOfMemory}`: the arena) draws a `T` from any source the
harnesses accept (`fuzz.Rng`, `std.testing.Smith`, `fuzz.ScriptSource`), so the
tape shrinker shrinks a failing struct: every draw is ordered so a zeroed tape
is the smallest value (`false`, `0`, first enum tag, `null`, empty slice, first
union tag). Mapping: `bool`; ints edge-biased (0, 1, -1 / max, min, max,
min+1, max-1 about one draw in nine, else uniform); floats edge-biased (0,
-0.0, ±1, ±inf, NaN unless `float_nan = false`, smallest subnormal and normal,
±max, small integers, else uniform bit patterns); enums (non-exhaustive: now and
then an unnamed value); `?T` (null 1 in 8); arrays, vectors, tuples, structs;
tagged unions (a drawn tag, then its payload); `void`; slices (`[]T`,
`[]const T`, `[:s]T`, length `0..max_len`, allocated in `arena`), `[]const u8`
as `.any`, `.ascii_printable` or `.utf8` (valid code points of every width, no
surrogates; `max_len` then counts code points). A struct, union or enum with a
`pub fn arbitrary(comptime S: type, src: *S, arena: std.mem.Allocator) Error!@This()`
decl uses it instead (proptest's `Arbitrary` impl, Hypothesis' `from_type`
registration). `ArbOptions`: `max_len` (16, under 2^20), `max_depth` (4; an
optional or a slice is one level, below `max_depth` optionals are `null` and
slices empty, so recursive types terminate), `bytes`, `float_nan`.

Pointers other than slices, untagged/extern/packed unions, sentinel-terminated
arrays, opaque, error sets, `anyframe` and comptime-only types are a compile
error that names the path (`Outer.field[]`) to the offending type.

## Inline snapshots with an update workflow

```zig
try testkit.expectSnapshot(@src(), "version 3", version_line);
try testkit.expectSnapshot(@src(),
    \\HTTP/1.1 200 OK
    \\content-length: 0
, response_head);
try testkit.expectSnapshotHex(@src(), "45000054", header_bytes);   // bytes; the literal may be split over lines
```

The expected value is a literal at the call site, directly after `@src()`: a
`"..."` string or `\\` multiline lines. A mismatch fails with the diff and the
command to accept it:

```
snapshot mismatch at frame_test.zig:42:32
  first difference: line 2, byte offset 17 (expected 31 bytes, got 31 bytes)
  expected: "content-length: 0"
  actual:   "content-length: 5"
  update: TESTKIT_SNAPSHOT=update <the command that ran this test> (e.g. TESTKIT_SNAPSHOT=update scripts/modtest <module>)
```

Text names the first differing **line** and both versions (escaped, at most 200
bytes); a value that ends early says which side ends and what the other
continues with. The hex form reuses the golden diff (`golden.diff`, `golden.render`):
a length mismatch, else the first differing offset with the bracketed window.

**Update mode.** `TESTKIT_SNAPSHOT=update` (any other non-empty value is an
error, so a typo cannot silently mean "compare") makes a mismatch rewrite the
literal in the source file and pass. The rewrite is atomic (temp file in the same
directory + rename, the file's permissions kept), keeps the indentation of the
call line and its line endings (LF or CRLF), and chooses the form: `"..."`
with escapes, or `\\` lines when the text has a newline, is valid UTF-8 and
holds no other control byte (a tab or carriage return would be at the tokenizer's
mercy). A hex snapshot of up to 32 bytes is one line, longer ones are split into
lines of 32 bytes. A fresh snapshot is `expectSnapshot(@src(), "", value)` and one
update run. Idempotence: the written literal decodes to exactly the value, so the
next run is a plain pass and nothing is rewritten. Review with `git diff`. The
run prints one `rewrote the snapshot at file:line` line per rewrite on stderr,
so a lane that fails on stderr (`scripts/modtest`) reports failure although the
rewrite happened; run it again without the variable.

**Finding the file.** `@src().file` is relative to the module root directory (the
directory of the module's root source file) and the test binary does not know
that directory. The path is searched from the repository root (the nearest
ancestor of the cwd with a `build.zig`) over `<root>/`, `<root>/src/` and, for
every module, `modules/<m>/{src,.,tools,example}/`; a candidate counts only if
the text at line:column is `@src()` followed by a literal that decodes to
**exactly the `expected` argument**. One match is used; none is
`error.SnapshotSourceNotFound`; several is `error.SnapshotAmbiguous`, ended by
`TESTKIT_SNAPSHOT_ROOT=modules/<m>/src` (relative to the repo root, no `..`). A
file name or override that is absolute or contains `..` is refused
(`error.SnapshotBadPath`), as is a non-`.zig` name, so nothing outside the
repository is opened for writing. When the literal is not directly after `@src()`
(`++`, an identifier, a trailing comment) the error is `error.SnapshotNotLiteral`;
when the text at the location is not `@src()` any more (the file was edited after
the build) it is `error.SnapshotSourceChanged`. Nothing is written in any of these
cases. A symbolic link in the tree is followed (not checked).

**Several snapshots in one run.** One file may hold many (also two on a line);
rewriting one moves the line numbers the compiled-in `@src()`s of the later ones
refer to. The first touch of a file keeps its original text; positions are
looked up in that original and shifted by the rewrites already made before them.
The same location reached twice with different values (a helper in a loop) is
`error.SnapshotConflict`, not a silent last write. Two update runs on the same
file at the same time are not supported.

**Bounds.** A source file over 4 MiB or an actual value over 1 MiB (update mode)
is `error.SnapshotTooLarge`; an allocation failure is `error.OutOfMemory`,
raised before anything is written, so the file is either untouched or complete.
Nothing here panics on any input.

There is no review mode: see *What is deliberately not done*.

## Faults drawn like any other choice

```zig
const plan = testkit.fuzz.FaultPlan.draw(src, input.len);
var r = testkit.fuzz.ChunkedReader.init(input, plan, &rbuf);   // short reads, ReadFailed at a byte
var w = testkit.fuzz.ChunkedWriter.init(&out, plan, &wbuf);    // short writes, WriteFailed at a byte
var fa = testkit.fuzz.failingAllocator(src, gpa, 32);          // half the time, fail from allocation k on
```

`Reader.fixed` and `Writer.Allocating` test the one transport that never
happens — everything at once, never an error. These put where the stream
breaks and where it fails into the input, so the driver explores them, a
seed replays them and the shrinker reduces them (one-byte chunks and a fault
at byte 0 are the small end). Only `valueRangeAtMost`/`value` are drawn, so
the harness also runs under `std.testing.Smith`.

## Guard pages

`testkit.guard.Guarded(cap).tail(len)` is `len` bytes ending at an
unreadable page, `head(len)` `len` bytes starting after one: a read past the
end (or before the start) faults under the seed that made it. A differential
fuzz cannot see such a read when every implementation compared shares the
code doing it, and a `[*]` read has no bounds check even in ReleaseSafe
(brotli 2026-10-15). One region per type, mapped once; a plain buffer off Linux.

## The comparison bench driver

Moved to its own module, [`benchkit`](../benchkit/README.md), on 2026-11-14: no
test imports it, and here each of its edits re-keyed 221 modules' tests.

## The golden diff

`std.testing.expectEqualSlices` prints both slices in full. For the goldens
this repo actually has — a 200-byte netlink datagram from `iproute2`, a GOOSE
frame, a DER certificate — that is two walls of hex and you still have to find
the difference by eye. `expectBytes` names the first differing **offset** and
shows a window around it with the offending byte bracketed:

```
golden differs at offset 44 (0x2c): expected 0x08, got 0x0c
  offset 36..
  expected:  00  00  01  00  00  00  00  00 [08] 00  01  00 ...
  actual:    00  00  01  00  00  00  00  00 [0c] 00  01  00 ...
```

A golden failure is nearly always "one field moved", and the offset names the
field. A **length** mismatch is reported separately and first: a truncated
encode is a different bug from a wrong byte, and conflating them costs a
debugging cycle.

The comparison (`diff`) and the formatting (`render`) are pure functions and
are what the tests exercise. That is not tidiness — a test asserting "this
comparison fails" would otherwise print its own diagnostic on every green run,
and this repo treats any stderr from the suite as a real problem.

## Open: the one thing not verified here

`verbose_skip_env`'s **value** — the string `"ZIG_LIBS_VERBOSE_SKIP"` — is not
pinned by any test, and cannot be: a test reading the same literal it checks is
circular, and a test binary cannot set a variable for itself. A typo would
silently mean "never verbose" forever. The decision *logic* is tested
(`verboseEnabled`); the name is held only by `scripts/test.sh` and the docs
using the same spelling. Grep before renaming.

## Verify

```
zig build test-testkit                          # Debug
zig build test-testkit -Doptimize=ReleaseFast   # ReleaseFast
zig build check-testonly                        # the isolation claim
zig build bench-testkit -Djcc-safe              # cost per input vs proptest, libFuzzer (needs cargo, clang)
TESTKIT_FUZZ=200000 zig build test-testkit -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe   # the fuzz verdict
```

The card's `**Audit:**` line is the current review and mutation score (cumulative over the last whole-module mutation
run and the delta runs after it).

`check-testonly` is the one worth knowing about. `test_deps` claims the published module never needs the harness, and
**nothing else checked that**: Zig analyses container-level decls lazily, so an unused `@import("testkit")` in a
module's non-test code is simply never looked at. The step forces the analysis with a consumer-shaped probe, so a
leak into published code fails it while that module's own `zig build test-<m>` stays green. Forcing that analysis also
compiles public code nothing had ever referenced.

Provenance: original work of the zig-libs authors (MIT); a thin layer over
`std.testing`. No third-party source consulted or copied, so no `NOTICE` entry
is required (root [`NOTICE`](../../NOTICE) §0). The bench's foreign sides
(`tools/proptest_rust`, `tools/libfuzzer_c`) are our own programs that link
proptest (MIT OR Apache-2.0, pinned `Cargo.lock`) and clang's libFuzzer
runtime (Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception) at bench time; nothing of either is
vendored or shipped. DATA: none. `src/golden.zig` is named for what it compares, not for what it holds — it is a diffing helper with no vendored bytes at all, and this module ships no test data, no fixture and no corpus of any kind. (The catalog gate's data-file check matches on the filename and so names this file; the answer is that there is nothing there.)

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class C · oracle n/a

- **Class C** — internal algorithm or data structure — no outside exists, so correctness is defined by invariants or a brute-force reference. Not anchor debt.
- **Oracle n/a** — class C/D carries no anchor debt, so there is no oracle grade to give.

**What the tests actually contain.** in-process test-utility layer over std.testing, no wire/crypto

**Reference-class check anyway:** `modules/testkit/tools/README.md` — even a class-C decision benefits from a second opinion; `hex.into`/`.alloc` match a from-scratch strict RFC 4648 decoder on all 16 276 exhaustive short inputs (0 diffs), and disagree with Python's own `bytes.fromhex` only on its whitespace leniency (255/16 276, all in the stricter direction).

## Performance

The bench is `zig build bench-testkit -Djcc-safe` (`tools/bench.zig`; needs `cargo`, for the crates pinned in
`tools/proptest_rust/Cargo.lock`, and `clang` with its libFuzzer runtime): the driver's cost per input against proptest
(the reference) and libFuzzer (the fastest candidate), in rows `hex`, `hex+seedfile`, `alloc` and `alloc+seedfile`,
ratios by wall time. The card's Performance line holds the figures (the card is authoritative).

The property is the same on every side: a byte string of at most 160 bytes mapped to hex digits and decoded; `alloc`
adds two heap allocations per input — through the driver's leak-checking `SafeAllocator` on our side, glibc `malloc` on
libFuzzer's. Ours and proptest draw lengths the same way (half up to 64 bytes, half up to 160).

libFuzzer is measured **at its cheapest**: the property is compiled out of its instrumentation (`noinline`,
`no_sanitize("coverage")`), so only its own loop — mutation, coverage collection over the callback, corpus upkeep — is
timed. Instrumented as a user would write it, its per-byte compare tracing dominates, a cost of the property's code, not
of the driver. Without the property's coverage it also keeps its inputs short (about 25 bytes on average against our
56, printed by the bench), which favours it again. The `alloc` rows are the only ones near 1.0: two allocations through
a leak-checking allocator per input against plain `malloc` on half the bytes. AFL++ is not measured: not installed
here, and its fork-server execution costs far more per input than an in-process loop. The driver renews its
`SafeAllocator` per batch (1024 seeds or 64 MiB allocated) and pins a leak on its seed through a counting
`SeedLedger`, so the per-seed allocator set-up does not dominate a cheap harness.

## Backlog / deferred

- **Regex-string strategy and strategy combinators** (proptest `"[a-z]+"`, Hypothesis `from_regex`, `prop_map`/`filter`):
  `arbitrary` ships the type mapping only. A regex strategy needs testkit → `regex`, a test-only module depending on a
  published one (`check-testonly` forbids the reverse; this would be the first edge from the harness into a library) —
  an owner question. Combinators: a type's own `arbitrary` decl covers the registered-strategy case; map/filter are a
  wrapper type away and not asked for.
- **Model-based (stateful) op-sequence harness** (`ops` vs a model, generic over Impl/Model; proptest-state-machine, Go
  `rapid`): many modules wrote a `model_test.zig` of their own, in shapes that differ. Count the shared part before
  adopting (this module's admission rule).
- **`stackprobe` is blind above the longest zero run** (found in the sealedbox delta review): residue is counted only
  below that run, so an inner burn in a dependency hides a missing outer burn in the entry point (sealedbox `seal` stayed
  green with its burn removed: the run began 2.1 KiB down). `sealedbox` pins `Report.burn_top` as a workaround. Wanted:
  an option stating the expected burn top. Other modules that nest burns have not been checked.
- **Mutant switch** (`testkit.mutant("id")` over one env var, for schemata runs): every mutation run re-writes the
  switch; the runners themselves stay disposable (CONVENTIONS §9). Admit once two runs would have used it.
- **Multiplexed cycle counter not detected** (found by a TLS server's bench): `Cycles.read` (now in `benchkit`, where
  the fix belongs) reads the raw count; when the PMU multiplexes (other perf users, the NMI watchdog, more events than
  counters) the count covers only part of the run and the best-of-rounds picks the undercount — a ratio by cycles then
  disagrees with wall time. Ideal: open with `PERF_FORMAT_TOTAL_TIME_ENABLED | _RUNNING` and treat `running <
  enabled` as no counter (wall time), on both sides (the C harness is copied per module, so the shared C block needs the
  same).
- **Shrinking a `std.testing.Smith` input** (`_INPUT`): the tape covers the driver's `Rng` only; a `--fuzz` crash input
  is replayed whole.
- **A build option handing each module's source directory to the test binary** would replace the snapshot update's
  candidate search over the tree (`expectHex` / `expectBytes` goldens have no update: their expected value is a hex
  string made from the capture tool; convert a call to `expectSnapshotHex` to get one).
- **Same signal ≠ same panic** (`shrink.zig` `tryTape`): a SIGABRT candidate is accepted whatever the panic said. Ideal:
  the child's panic handler writes the message (or the first return address) into the shared mapping, compared like the
  error name. Needs a panic hook in the test root — it is the consumer's root, not ours.
- **A run that selects no harness is green** (`<PREFIX>_ONLY=typo`): every harness skips. Ideal: the per-core runner
  requires one `DONE <name>` line per expected harness; the driver alone cannot know the expected set.
- **Stack-probe secrets too short or too uniform for a needle window** count in `Report.unprobed_secrets` and print a
  warning; make it an error once a tag lane shows how many of the 287 calling files would trip.
- **Two jobs given the same `<PREFIX>_SEEDFILE`** truncate each other's mapping → SIGBUS (docs: one file per job).
- **`stackprobe` paints `Config.window` below the stack pointer** without checking the stack size (a small thread stack
  faults).
- **A `prefix` over ~85 bytes** overflows `env()`'s key buffer → the variable is silently ignored.
- **Smaller:** reach counters not atomic and the 48-label cap silent (`hit`); the process-global `dog_running` is wrong
  in a forked child that ran no watchdog of its own; `guard` regions are not cleared between seeds; a hand-built
  `FaultPlan` with a zero chunk reads 0 forever and `failingAllocator` never fails `resize`/`remap`; `bench` (now in `benchkit`) keeps only
  the last round's count, reports a worst ratio of 0 when every row is filtered out, and parses `nan`/`inf` and empty
  fields in a foreign row; `child`'s no-pidfd fallback returns `WaitFailed` unreaped and does not kill the child's own
  descendants.
